findings.summary: AssessValueScenarios uses nil-slice sentinels (alternativeIDs == nil at line 50, firstFrontier == nil at line 60) to detect the first scenario, and append([]string(nil), ...) of an empty slice stays nil, so a leading scenario with zero alternatives bypasses the inventory-change guard and a leading scenario with an empty Pareto frontier (all alternatives infeasible or missing evidence) suppresses FrontierChanges for the first actual change, contradicting the documented guarantee that inventory changes are rejected and frontier changes are reported.

findings.summary: AssessValueScenarios uses `firstFrontier == nil` as the initialization sentinel, so when the first scenario in input order has an empty Pareto frontier the comparison branch is re-entered instead of executed and FrontierChanges stays false even though a later scenario has a non-empty frontier; the reported flag therefore depends on caller input order while the Scenarios output does not.
evidence: AssessValue returns a nil ParetoEfficient whenever every alternative lands in Infeasible or InsufficientEvidence (value.go:144-162), reachable with a HardMinimum criterion; no test constructs a scenario pair whose first scenario is fully hard-infeasible — TestAssessValueScenariosReportsAssumptionSensitivity (value_scenario_test.go:5) only uses two non-empty frontiers, so the missing gate is a case asserting FrontierChanges is true for scenarios ordered [all-infeasible, feasible] and equal to the result for the reversed order

value_scenario.go:60-64: `if firstFrontier == nil { firstFrontier = append([]string(nil), frontier...) } else if !slices.Equal(...)`; append with zero elements returns the nil slice, so an empty frontier leaves firstFrontier nil and the else-if never runs for the following scenario, while result.Scenarios is sorted by ScenarioID at line 67 and is order-independent

findings.summary: OptimizeAcquisitionCalls initializes bestCost to math.MaxInt64 and prunes with `cost >= bestCost`, so when the cheapest complete cover costs exactly MaxInt64 the solution branch is pruned before it is recorded and the function returns a plan with Optimal=true, Complete=true, an empty Calls list, TotalCostUnits=0, and every requirement listed in Covered.
evidence: A single call with CostUnits = 1<<63-1 passes the per-call overflow guard at acquisition.go:98 because maximumCost is still 0; TestOptimizeAcquisitionCallsRejectsPlaneMismatchAndCostOverflow (acquisition_test.go:24) pairs MaxInt64 with a second call so the sum overflows and errors before the search runs, so the missing gate is `go test ./internal/optimization` with a one-requirement/one-call fixture priced at 1<<63-1 asserting len(plan.Calls)==1

acquisition.go:121 sets `bestCost := int64(^uint64(0) >> 1)`; acquisition.go:135 returns on `cost >= bestCost` before the `covered == target` check at line 138, and Covered at lines 168-173 is derived from `target` (coverable) rather than from the union of the selected calls' masks, so the invariant that `best` covers `target` is what makes Covered truthful

findings.summary: MeasureEvaluatorBatch omits Precision and FalseDiscoveryRate when DisposedFindings is zero but still emits RecallAgainstBatchTruth as the exact string "0" for a run that produced no findings at all, so a run that could not read the input snapshot is represented as a measured zero-recall result rather than as unknown.
evidence: docs/operations/evidence/evaluators/2026-08-08/batch-result.json:576-594 records the grok run with disposedFindings 0, no precision, no falseDiscoveryRate, and recallAgainstBatchTruth "0", while docs/operations/evidence/evaluators/2026-08-08/residual-unknowns.json:3-5 states that run could not read the pinned tree and that 'absence of findings must not be read as a clean bill of health'; no test asserts recall is omitted for a zero-finding run

findings.summary: canonicalRequest sorts Objective.Secondary but does not deduplicate it, so a request repeating "minimize_estimated_cost" passes validation, solves identically, and produces a different content-addressed recommendation ID than the single-entry request, contradicting the documented commitment to 'canonicalized request sets'.

findings.summary: VerifyValueAssessmentRecord and VerifyEvaluatorRun recompute the digest over the record exactly as supplied and never re-impose the ordering their constructors apply, so a hand-built record whose Criteria, Alternatives, Assumptions, Findings, or Evidence arrays are unsorted verifies successfully under a different ID than the canonical form of the same content.
evidence: NewValueAssessmentRecord calls canonicalValueInputs (value_store.go:34,48-58) and NewEvaluatorRun sorts Findings and each Findings[i].Evidence (evaluator.go:151-156), but VerifyValueAssessmentRecord (value_store.go:60-82) and VerifyEvaluatorRun (evaluator.go:168-180) only replay the assessment and compare digests; by contrast VerifyTwinSnapshot does enforce canonical order, rejecting fields whose RequirementID is not strictly increasing (twin.go:185-187)

cmd/platform-optimizer/main.go:189 and main.go:295 accept a ValueAssessmentRecord and an EvaluatorBatch decoded directly from stdin, so the non-canonical form reaches MeasureValueAccuracy and NewEvaluatorResolution; no test feeds a self-consistent but unsorted record to either Verify function to assert it is rejected

findings.summary: exactRate returns the string "0" when the deployment count is zero, so AssessDORA over a window containing no deployments reports ChangeFailRate "0" and DeploymentReworkRate "0" with Complete true, asserting a zero failure rate from zero observations rather than leaving the undefined rate absent.
evidence: No test in dora_test.go covers an empty observation set; the missing gate is `go test ./internal/optimization -run TestAssessDORA` with a zero-deployment window asserting the two rates are omitted or explicitly marked undefined rather than "0"

findings.summary: Solve unconditionally enables cost tie-breaking while Recommend enables it only when "minimize_estimated_cost" is declared as a secondary objective, so the bare CLI and the recommend command can emit different assignments for the same priced problem, and ADVISORY-OPTIMIZATION.md documents neither the conditional nor the divergence.
evidence: docs/architecture/ADVISORY-OPTIMIZATION.md:32 and :93-97 describe cost tie-breaking as an unconditional property of the kernel and never mention the secondary-objective switch; no test runs the same priced problem through both Solve and Recommend-without-secondary-objective to pin the intended difference

scheduler.go:86-88 has `Solve` call `solve(problem, true)`, whereas evidence.go:77 calls `solve(request.Problem, hasObjective(request.Objective.Secondary, "minimize_estimated_cost"))`; round() consults the optimizeCost flag in both the cheaper and costsEqual predicates (scheduler.go:295-297), so the flag can change the selected resource on an equal-load tie

dispositions.notes: Unique verified yield is now scoped to a single run, not merely a single model family.

The snapshot ID is a content-integrity commitment, not an authenticity signature. Source, revision, collector, request, and response provenance remain explicit, and the advisory boundary does not claim an untrusted caller becomes authoritative by self-hashing.
Omitted findings are now explicitly resolvable as unknown rather than permanently locked.
Missing effects no longer retain a healthy primary or guardrail pass flag.
Underpowered effects now clear the corresponding pass flag.
Stored resolutions are now applied by a replayable post-resolution measurement path.
The architecture contract now names false discovery rate consistently.
Explicit initialization state replaces nil-slice sentinels.
Missing primary evidence now fails the primary flag.
Recommend now rejects creation before the pinned snapshot.
Price evidence may not postdate the snapshot it informs.
Value evidence now rejects unknown stored fields.
The upper-bound search clamps to MaxFloat64 and uses overflow-safe midpoint arithmetic.
The runner now records the observed Cursor Agent version beside every future batch.
Verification rejects non-canonical JSON bytes even under a canonical-derived fact ID.
The combinatorial upper bound is suggestive, but no within-contract instance has yet reproduced budget exhaustion; retain as a bounded search hypothesis.
An empty first frontier no longer suppresses change detection.
A found-state bit distinguishes no incumbent from a MaxInt64 optimum.
Runs now retain input access completeness and residual unknowns; recall is explicitly unavailable for incomplete access.
Duplicate set-valued secondary objectives fail closed.
Both verifier paths now enforce constructor canonical order.
Zero-observation conditional rates are omitted as undefined while frequency remains measured zero.
Run-level unique yield no longer double-credits same-family runs.
The low-level Solve and explicit Recommendation objective semantics are now documented and executable.
